newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Dalai Lama asks prayers for doomed Taiwan pigs.
newsitem.headline: Dalai Lama asks prayers for doomed Taiwan pigs.

text.p: Tibet's exiled spiritual leader the Dalai Lama on Wednesday jumped into the fray over Taiwan's hog epidemic -- pledging to pray for the doomed pigs' souls.
The visiting Tibetan god-king said he was concerned about the island-wide foot and mouth disease outbreak that was likely to result in the death or slaughter of up to 1.6 million pigs.

"I heard that the condition was serious and many pigs had to be buried alive," the ochre-robed monk told state radio on the fifth day of a six-day Taiwan tour. "I hope everybody can get together and pray for their samsara (transmigration)."
Taiwan television has shown graphic scenes of diseased pigs being buried alive in giant pits at farms lacking the means to electrocute and incinerate them.
He urged people to eat less meat and more vegetables instead -- a recommendation unlikely to go down well with Taiwan's distraught hog farmers.
Unlike many of Taiwan's Buddhists, the Dalai Lama is not a vegetarian but tries to eat as little meat as possible.
The government has ordered the destruction of all pigs, even healthy ones, at farms affected by the epidemic.
